title: US Measles Cases Head for Highest Level Since 1991
summaryZh: 美國今年麻疹逾4400例，可望創1991年來新高，賓州疫情最重。
summaryHi: अमेरिका में इस साल खसरे के 4,400 से अधिक मामले, 1991 के बाद सबसे ज़्यादा होने की राह पर।
summaryEs: EE. UU. supera los 4.400 casos de sarampión este año, camino de su máximo desde 1991.
summaryJa: 米国の麻疹患者が今年4400人超、1991年以来の最多に迫る。

summaryEn: The US has had over 4,400 measles cases this year, the most since 1991, with a big outbreak in Pennsylvania.

sources.name: Business Today (CDC and Pennsylvania Department of Health data)

paragraphs: Measles cases in the United States are heading for their highest annual total since 1991, according to the latest data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
By Thursday, 4,410 confirmed cases had been recorded in 2026, nearly double the 2,289 reported throughout 2025. They were spread across 47 jurisdictions, and 18 involved international visitors.

Children and teenagers account for the largest share, with 1,856 cases, or 42%, among people aged 5 to 19. Roughly 10% of patients have been admitted to hospital, and about 96% were either unvaccinated or had an unknown vaccination status.

Pennsylvania is at the centre of the surge. Its health department has confirmed 1,260 cases across 43 counties this year, along with 238 hospitalisations and five measles-related deaths, and it is investigating another death in Franklin County. The CDC is deploying an Epidemic Intelligence Service officer to support the state.
Health officials stress that two doses of the MMR vaccine offer the strongest protection, and that community immunity works best when more than 95% of people are vaccinated.
Measles is an illness that spreads very easily. In the United States, many more people have it this year.
There are 4,410 cases so far in 2026. Last year there were 2,289 cases. This year may have the most cases since 1991.
Many sick people are children and teenagers. About 1 in 10 sick people went to hospital. Almost all of them did not have the vaccine, or nobody knows.
The state of Pennsylvania has the biggest problem. It has 1,260 cases, and five people have died. A health expert from the national health agency is going there to help.
Doctors say two doses of the MMR vaccine are the best way to stay safe.
The United States is on track to have its highest number of measles cases since 1991, according to new figures from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
As of Thursday, the CDC had counted 4,410 confirmed cases this year, almost twice the 2,289 cases reported in the whole of 2025. Cases have come from 47 areas of the country.
Young people have been hit hardest: 42% of patients were aged 5 to 19. About one in ten patients needed hospital care, and around 96% were unvaccinated or did not know if they had been vaccinated.
Pennsylvania has the worst outbreak. The state has reported 1,260 cases in 43 counties, 238 hospital stays and five deaths. The CDC is sending a disease expert to help local health officials.

The CDC says two doses of the MMR vaccine give the best protection, and doctors are asking parents to check that their children have had both doses. When more than 95% of a community is vaccinated, it is much harder for the disease to spread.
Measles cases in the United States are heading for their highest annual total since 1991, according to the latest data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
By Thursday, 4,410 confirmed cases had been recorded in 2026, nearly double the 2,289 reported throughout 2025. They were spread across 47 jurisdictions, and 18 involved international visitors.

Children and teenagers account for the largest share, with 1,856 cases, or 42%, among people aged 5 to 19. Roughly 10% of patients have been admitted to hospital, and about 96% were either unvaccinated or had an unknown vaccination status.

Pennsylvania is at the centre of the surge. Its health department has confirmed 1,260 cases across 43 counties this year, along with 238 hospitalisations and five measles-related deaths, and it is investigating another death in Franklin County. The CDC is deploying an Epidemic Intelligence Service officer to support the state.
Health officials stress that two doses of the MMR vaccine offer the strongest protection, and that community immunity works best when more than 95% of people are vaccinated.
The United States is on course to record more measles infections this year than in any year since 1991, underlining how far a disease once considered under control has staged a comeback.

Figures from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) show 4,410 confirmed cases as of Thursday, almost double the 2,289 logged in the whole of 2025. Infections have been reported in 47 jurisdictions, with 18 involving international visitors.

The burden has fallen disproportionately on the young, with 42% of cases among those aged 5 to 19. Around one in ten patients has required hospital treatment, and some 96% of those infected were unvaccinated or of unknown vaccination status.

Pennsylvania has emerged as the epicentre, with 1,260 confirmed cases across 43 counties, 238 hospitalisations and five deaths so far; officials are also examining a further suspected death in Franklin County. The CDC is dispatching an Epidemic Intelligence Service officer to reinforce the state's response.
Public health authorities reiterate that two doses of the MMR vaccine remain the most effective defence, and that community immunity holds only when vaccination coverage exceeds 95%.

The United States is poised to record its highest annual number of measles cases since 1991, a development that highlights the resurgence of a highly contagious disease previously regarded as largely eliminated.

According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), 4,410 confirmed cases had been documented by Thursday, almost twice the 2,289 recorded throughout 2025. These cases were distributed across 47 jurisdictions, and 18 involved international visitors.

Younger people have been disproportionately affected, with individuals aged 5 to 19 accounting for 42% of infections. Approximately 10% of patients have required hospitalisation, and an overwhelming 96% were either unvaccinated or of unknown vaccination status.

Pennsylvania constitutes the epicentre of the outbreak, having confirmed 1,260 cases in 43 counties, 238 hospitalisations and five fatalities this year, while a further death in Franklin County is under investigation. Consequently, the CDC is deploying a specialist from its Epidemic Intelligence Service to assist state authorities.
Health officials emphasise that two doses of the MMR vaccine constitute the most effective safeguard, and that community immunity can only be sustained when vaccination coverage surpasses 95%.
